findings.title: Mixed cash/electronic checkout cannot confirm its electronic leg

acceptance_criteria: Each tender leg can complete independently and exactly once.
Confirmed electronic state and its movement commit atomically; channel totals reconcile.

findings.title: Distinct concurrent business-day opens can pass pre-insert active-state validation
findings.disposition_rationale: Static source code shows plausible concurrency/SQL race condition; complete physical proof requires concurrent multi-threaded SQL Server test harness.
findings.root_cause: Active-day admission is a read-check-insert invariant. OpenBusinessDayHandler reads current active rows and invokes BusinessDayRules.Open before a separate insert; there is no shared transaction/conditional state claim, while the schema has uniqueness only by request ID.
findings.impact: More than one active business day may be persisted, making day attribution, financial close blockers/snapshots, and active-day lookups ambiguous. No actual duplicate day or accounting loss has been reproduced.
findings.remediation_plan: Modify affected handler to enforce proper invariant and transaction boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: A documented owner policy establishes the active-day scope (global or per defined partition).

If global single-active-day remains intended, every Open/Reopen transition is serialized or constrained by database-enforced uniqueness so concurrent instances cannot persist more than one active day.
A losing concurrency attempt leaves no partial state and the existing same-request replay contract remains intact.

findings.title: Delivery report field labeled expected unsettled custody aggregates collected amount instead
findings.disposition_rationale: Static source code shows plausible concurrency/SQL race condition; complete physical proof requires concurrent multi-threaded SQL Server test harness.
findings.root_cause: Delivery report field labeled expected unsettled custody aggregates collected amount instead
findings.impact: If the DTO/UI contract means expected cash at driver risk, the report underreports that exposure while delivery is in transit and diverges from the owner dashboard. If it intentionally means cash already collected but not settled, the aggregation may be deliberate but DTO name and tests are misleading. No loss, duplicate payment, or ledger corruption is established.
findings.remediation_plan: Modify affected handler to enforce proper invariant and transaction boundaries.
acceptance_criteria: DTO field name and source aggregate express the same amount.
Owner dashboard and delivery report agree for the same non-settled custody cohort when they claim to show expected custody.
In-transit and variance cases are covered by tests; no real printer or financial operation is needed.
Historical statement temporal semantics are documented separately.
Before delivery, delivery report and owner dashboard agree on expected cash responsibility for the same open custody cohort while collected remains zero.
